findings.description: IS-011 + IS-012 (test scenarios I authored at /ases-integration-test Step A) used absolute dates (2026-06-05, 2026-05-28) that fell outside AC-021's 7-day backdate window when executed 24+ days later. The bug was 100% test-side and was caught by InwardService's AC-021 422 response — exactly the right behavior. Fixed in 1 iteration each by switching to date.today()-relative arithmetic with month-boundary handling.
findings.lessons_learned: Future Step-A scenario designers should default to relative-date arithmetic; absolute dates in test fixtures are fragile across run dates.
findings.process_improvement: Could add a scenario-design lint that flags absolute dates in integration_scenarios.json file paths — not a sprint blocker.

findings.description: TC-122 (dashboard perf gate) was initially miscoded — synthetic ledger seed used `running_balance = 500 + month_offset * 10` per-month reset + day_offset % 28 modulo, producing non-cumulative balances that violated FORMULA-001 on every read. Production code's invariant assertion correctly caught it. Fixed at /ases-test-run iteration 1.
findings.lessons_learned: Production-level invariants (FORMULA-001 server-side assert) successfully caught a test-side data corruption. This is the defense-in-depth pattern working as designed; in fact, DS-016 ledger-corruption signal documentation was on point. The fix went into the test seed, not the SUT.

findings.description: AC-049 ('both sections render together on the same screen') was accepted as a backend dual-payload contract; the full visual verification of 'no toggle, no tab, Consolidation first' awaits /ases-ui-scaffold S3. This is by design — backend sprint scope ends at the JSON contract level.
